a.raw: when edmund saw the lion he stood very still
a.fixed: When Edmund saw the lion, he stood very still.
a.why: When starts the part that cannot stand alone, so a comma goes after lion. Saw and stood are irregular past verbs.

b.raw: when the wolf stood up edmund began to tremble
b.fixed: When the wolf stood up, Edmund began to tremble.
b.why: When starts the part that cannot stand alone, so a comma goes after up. Edmund is a name. Stood and began are irregular past verbs.

cards.title: World Notes: Stone Statues
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapter with your lens in mind.
text: Real statues are carved by artists from stone, like marble or granite.
Some old castles and gardens have courtyards full of statues of people and animals.
In the story, the Witch's statues were once living creatures. That part is only in the story.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. Edmund is alone in the snow. Watch what he tells himself in Chapter 9, and what he really knows.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: build not words, fix a sentence's verbs, and proofread prefix words.
transcripts.guide2: Read Chapter 9. Then answer three questions.
transcripts.guide3: Today you make your comparison more precise.

notes.wordParts: The word parts in- and im- both mean not. inactive = not active. impolite = not polite. Use im- before words that start with m or p.
notes.grammar: An irregular verb does not add -ed for the past. You learn each one: say → said, see → saw, sit → sat.
notes.spelling: A prefix goes on the front of a base word, and the base word keeps its spelling. Peel the prefix off to read the base: un + happy.
notes.wgrd: Edmund tells himself the Witch is the rightful Queen, but deep down he knows she is bad and cruel.
vocab: the right or power to give orders and make decisions
a statement that something will happen in the future
to be disloyal to someone who trusted you
betraying someone's trust in a very serious way

mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. The correct one first. When Edmund came to the lion, he felt cold stone and knew that it was only a statue. A comma comes after the when part. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.script: Snap the parts together. Im. Mature. Immature! Immature means not grown up yet, like a puppy chewing your shoes. Say each pair of parts out loud. Type the whole word in the box. Then tap Check My Answers.

mods.todo: Read each sentence. Pick the word that fits.
mods.script: Try each word in the blank, and keep the one that makes sense. Here's my sentence. The children ate dinner in the Beavers' blank little house. Treachery? Hmm, no. Snug? Yes! Now pick the word that fits each sentence.

mods.todo: Read the before and after. Fix the sentence and list three more verbs like these.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence the way the editor did. Mr. Beaver keeped a hole open in the ice. Keeped? The past of keep is kept. Mr. Beaver kept a hole open in the ice. Read the before and after, and tap Check yourself. Then fix the sentence, and list three more verbs like these.

mods.todo: Read the rule. Tap a word to check it. Find the two mistakes in each sentence.
mods.script: Proofreader time! Here's a word with a mistake. Unsaif. Peel off the front part. What's left should be safe: s, a, f, e. The base word never changes, so it's unsafe. Read the rule. Then tap the words you think are spelled wrong.

virtue.name: honesty
virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: Edmund tells himself the Witch is the rightful Queen, but deep down he knows she is bad and cruel.
items.why: He is not being honest with himself.

items.t: Edmund thinks more and more that he hates Peter, as if the cold and the snow were Peter's fault.
items.why: Blaming Peter for his own choice is not honest.

items.t: Edmund tells the Witch that his brother and sisters are at the Beavers' house.
items.why: He tells the truth, but he uses it to help the Witch. Honest words can still hurt people.
